#====================================================================================================
# START - Testing Protocol - DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE THIS SECTION
#====================================================================================================

# THIS SECTION CONTAINS CRITICAL TESTING INSTRUCTIONS FOR BOTH AGENTS
# BOTH MAIN_AGENT AND TESTING_AGENT MUST PRESERVE THIS ENTIRE BLOCK

# Communication Protocol:
# If the `testing_agent` is available, main agent should delegate all testing tasks to it.
#
# You have access to a file called `test_result.md`. This file contains the complete testing state
# and history, and is the primary means of communication between main and the testing agent.
#
# Main and testing agents must follow this exact format to maintain testing data. 
# The testing data must be entered in yaml format Below is the data structure:
# 
## user_problem_statement: {problem_statement}
## backend:
##   - task: "Task name"
##     implemented: true
##     working: true  # or false or "NA"
##     file: "file_path.py"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"  # or "medium" or "low"
##     needs_retesting: false
##     status_history:
##         -working: true  # or false or "NA"
##         -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##         -comment: "Detailed comment about status"
##
## frontend:
##   - task: "Task name"
##     implemented: true
##     working: true  # or false or "NA"
##     file: "file_path.js"
##     stuck_count: 0
##     priority: "high"  # or "medium" or "low"
##     needs_retesting: false
##     status_history:
##         -working: true  # or false or "NA"
##         -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##         -comment: "Detailed comment about status"
##
## metadata:
##   created_by: "main_agent"
##   version: "1.0"
##   test_sequence: 0
##   run_ui: false
##
## test_plan:
##   current_focus:
##     - "Task name 1"
##     - "Task name 2"
##   stuck_tasks:
##     - "Task name with persistent issues"
##   test_all: false
##   test_priority: "high_first"  # or "sequential" or "stuck_first"
##
## agent_communication:
##     -agent: "main"  # or "testing" or "user"
##     -message: "Communication message between agents"

# Protocol Guidelines for Main agent
#
# 1. Update Test Result File Before Testing:
#    - Main agent must always update the `test_result.md` file before calling the testing agent
#    - Add implementation details to the status_history
#    - Set `needs_retesting` to true for tasks that need testing
#    - Update the `test_plan` section to guide testing priorities
#    - Add a message to `agent_communication` explaining what you've done
#
# 2. Incorporate User Feedback:
#    - When a user provides feedback that something is or isn't working, add this information to the relevant task's status_history
#    - Update the working status based on user feedback
#    - If a user reports an issue with a task that was marked as working, increment the stuck_count
#    - Whenever user reports issue in the app, if we have testing agent and task_result.md file so find the appropriate task for that and append in status_history of that task to contain the user concern and problem as well 
#
# 3. Track Stuck Tasks:
#    - Monitor which tasks have high stuck_count values or where you are fixing same issue again and again, analyze that when you read task_result.md
#    - For persistent issues, use websearch tool to find solutions
#    - Pay special attention to tasks in the stuck_tasks list
#    - When you fix an issue with a stuck task, don't reset the stuck_count until the testing agent confirms it's working
#
# 4. Provide Context to Testing Agent:
#    - When calling the testing agent, provide clear instructions about:
#      - Which tasks need testing (reference the test_plan)
#      - Any authentication details or configuration needed
#      - Specific test scenarios to focus on
#      - Any known issues or edge cases to verify
#
# 5. Call the testing agent with specific instructions referring to test_result.md
#
# IMPORTANT: Main agent must ALWAYS update test_result.md BEFORE calling the testing agent, as it relies on this file to understand what to test next.

#====================================================================================================
# END - Testing Protocol - DO NOT EDIT OR REMOVE THIS SECTION
#====================================================================================================

FIX APPLIED: (1) Concurrency semaphore (EXPORT_RENDER_CONCURRENCY=2) to serialize heavy renders, (2) Memory-lean Chromium flags (--js-flags=--max-old-space-size=512, --disable-extensions, etc.), (3) Infrastructure bumps (memory 2Gi→4Gi, cpu 2→4, max-instances 3→10), (4) Nginx timeout increases (proxy_read_timeout 120s→300s).         comment: "✅ PDF EXPORT ROUND-4 WBS CLIPPING FIX VERIFIED (Sep 25, 2026): Comprehensive verification of ROUND-4 structural fix in WBSView.js performed with 4/4 tests passed (100% success rate). CONTEXT: The ROUND-3 print.css fix (zeroing min-widths) helped but WBS table rightmost columns were STILL clipped in some cases. ROOT CAUSE: The read-only (client report / PDF) plan table was using `overflow-x-auto` + `min-w-max` which forced the table wider than the page, causing rightmost columns to clip.         comment: "FIX APPLIED: Updated _dt() helper in /app/backend/services/status_drafter.py (lines 35-48) to normalize BOTH naive strings and naive datetimes to UTC-aware. For datetime objects: checks if x.tzinfo exists; if not, adds timezone.utc (line 47). This ensures ALL datetimes are normalized to UTC-aware before comparison operations in _snapshot function (lines 59, 87, 92, 100, 104), preventing the 'can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware' TypeError. Implementation: WBS endpoints (GET /api/projects/{pid}/wbs, /wbs/budget-status, /wbs/actuals, /wbs/tasks-for-timesheet, /wbs/summary) now call check_project_read_access(current_user, project_id) which enforces role-aware scoping. Baseline endpoints (GET /api/projects/{pid}/baselines, /baselines/current, /baselines/{bid}, /variance, /variance/{bid}, /change-log) now call get_user_allowed_project_ids_read(current_user) which returns None for admin/resource (unrestricted), set of allowed projects for contractor/client. WRITE endpoints (POST/PUT/DELETE) remain admin/lead gated via _require_admin_or_project_lead() - NO CHANGES to write permissions."

metadata:
  created_by: "main_agent"
  version: "1.0"
  test_sequence: 13
  run_ui: false

test_plan:
  current_focus:
    - "AI Summary/Chat Path Fix (Gemini Provider Hardening)"
  stuck_tasks: []
  test_all: false
  test_priority: "high_first"

agent_communication:
  - agent: "main"
    message: "PDF EXPORT 502/OOM HARDENING — needs verification. PROD ROOT CAUSE (from Cloud Run logs): heavy headless-Chromium report renders were OOM-killing the 2Gi instance; while it restarted, ALL concurrent requests (even trivial /api/notifications polls) returned instant ~1ms 502s. The frontend then fell back to a crude client-side html2canvas slicer producing the 'unclean' PDF. FIXES APPLIED: (1) backend/services/exports/renderer.py — added a global asyncio.Semaphore (EXPORT_RENDER_CONCURRENCY, default 1, prod=2) that SERIALISES heavy renders so concurrent exports can't stack Chromium memory and OOM the container; added memory-lean Chromium flags (--js-flags=--max-old-space-size=512, disable-extensions, etc.); page.close() in finally. (2) cloudbuild.yaml — memory 2Gi->4Gi, cpu 2->4, max-instances 3->10, EXPORT_RENDER_CONCURRENCY=2. (3) nginx.conf — /api proxy_read_timeout 120s->300s (match Cloud Run) so long renders aren't cut to 504; stopped retrying http_502 on the single crashed upstream. (4) frontend ProjectReport.js — rewrote exportClientSidePDF fallback to paginate at natural SECTION boundaries (cover/summary/timeline/overview/budget/risks/wbs) so even the fallback is clean (no mid-section cut, full width, no blank page); softened UX toast to 'Preparing your PDF…'. (5) api.js — export calls pass skipErrorToast so a 502 flash isn't shown before the fallback runs. PLEASE TEST backend: GET /api/projects/6ab25bc82be78e05e89230f3/export/pdf (Website Redesign has 8 WBS tasks + 4 risks). Verify: (a) HTTP 200 valid PDF 16:9 (960x540), multi-page, WBS 'ACTUALS VS EST'/DEPS fully visible, no clipping, no blank trailing page (render pages with pdftoppm). (b) Fire 3 CONCURRENT export requests — ALL must return HTTP 200 with the FULL ~1.2MB PDF (NOT the tiny ~4KB ReportLab fallback), proving the semaphore serialises without failing. (c) Regression: /api/projects/{id}/export/ppt returns 200 valid PPTX; /api/health 200; /api/projects returns 4. NOTE: local env sets FRONTEND_INTERNAL_URL=http://localhost:3000 so the renderer reaches the dev server (preview has no nginx:8080); this is local-only and does not affect prod."
  - agent: "testing"
    message: "✅ PDF CLEAN-LAYOUT FIX VERIFICATION COMPLETE (Sep 22, 2026): All layout issues have been successfully fixed. Comprehensive testing performed on project 6ab25bc82be78e05e89230f3 with 8 WBS tasks (long names) + 4 risks (long descriptions). RESULTS: (1) HTTP 200 ✅, valid PDF 1195.6 KB ✅, Content-Type application/pdf ✅, PDF magic bytes verified ✅. (2) Page count: 6 pages ✅, Page size: 960x540 pts (16:9) ✅. (3) VISUAL VERIFICATION via pdftoppm PNG renders: (a) WBS table rightmost columns ('ACTUALS VS EST.' showing '0h / 8h' etc, 'DEPS' showing '—') are FULLY VISIBLE with NO right-edge clipping ✅. (4) PPT regression test: GET /api/projects/6ab25bc82be78e05e89230f3/export/ppt returns HTTP 200 with 844.1 KB valid PPTX (8 slides) ✅. FINAL VERDICT: ALL 4 LAYOUT ISSUES FIXED. The renderer.py fix (prefer_css_page_size=True + zero margins) and print.css fixes (width-clamping, table-layout:fixed, word-break, footer page-break-before:avoid) work perfectly.     message: "PROD BUG: report Status Summary shows 'Could not parse structured summary — I'm unable to process your request. Please check AI configuration'. CAUSE: user switched prod AI from Emergent to Gemini (removed EMERGENT_LLM_KEY env, needs GEMINI_API_KEY). The /api/ai/chat path (used by the report summary) calls get_ai_config()->call_gemini_api; when Gemini fails AND EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is absent, it returns the generic 'unable to process' message. The OLD call_gemini_api had a 15s timeout (too short for long report prompts) and no error logging / no model fallback, so failures were silent.   - agent: "user"
    message: "Verify a bug fix on the AI 'draft status update' endpoint in DD Planner (FastAPI). Respond in English only. Real AI key (EMERGENT_LLM_KEY) is configured — do NOT mock. WHAT WAS FIXED: POST /api/ai/draft-status-update/{project_id} was returning HTTP 500 with 'TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes'. Root cause: the _dt() helper in /app/backend/services/status_drafter.py returned NAIVE datetimes when parsing stored ISO date strings that had no timezone (e.g. '2025-07-01T00:00:00'), which then failed comparison against timezone-aware now/since. The helper now normalizes BOTH naive strings and naive datetimes to UTC-aware. AUTH: Login as admin@test.com / admin123. TESTS: (1) Find a real project id (GET /api/projects → pick one; prefer one that has WBS tasks and/or timesheets so the datetime comparisons are actually exercised — the seed project 'QA Test Project - My Allocations' has phases with naive date strings like 2025-07-01T00:00:00 and is a GOOD candidate to trigger the original bug). (2) POST /api/ai/draft-status-update/{project_id} with the appropriate body (inspect /app/backend/routes/ai_productivity.py for the exact request schema/params; send a minimal valid body). (3) Assert the response is HTTP 200 (NOT 500) and returns a coherent drafted status update payload. (4) Run it against at LEAST two different projects (including the QA seed project with naive date strings) to be confident the timezone fix holds across data shapes. (5) Check /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log for any new 'can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware' or ResponseValidationError during these calls — there must be NONE. REGRESSION: Also re-hit two previously-passing AI endpoints to ensure the restart/fix didn't regress anything: GET /api/ai/portfolio-budget-analysis → 200, POST /api/ai/kickoff-suggest (minimal valid body) → 200. REPORT BACK: HTTP status for draft-status-update on each project tested, and whether a coherent draft was returned. Confirm NO naive/aware datetime errors in logs during the test. Regression results for the two endpoints."

ROOT CAUSE: List view renders tasks using topoSortedTasks (topological sort by dependencies and start dates), but Move Up/Down operations use getSiblings() which sorts by the 'order' field. These produce DIFFERENT orderings. IMPACT: When user clicks Move Down on Task 1 (visually followed by Task 3), the system swaps Task 1 with Task 6 (next in order field sort), not Task 3. The UI doesn't update because topological order is unchanged. Network analysis confirms API calls succeed (PUT requests return 200, GET refetch returns 200), but the visual order remains unchanged. FIX REQUIRED: Ensure Move Up/Down operations work on the VISUAL order (topoSortedTasks) that users see, not the order field sort. Options: (1) Change getSiblings() to return siblings in topoSorted order, OR (2) Change List view to render by order field instead of topoSortedTasks, OR (3) Update order field to match topoSorted positions after refetch. See detailed analysis in task status_history. Priority: HIGH - this breaks core WBS functionality."

(4) Click Move Up to restore. (5) Indent test: click second task's Indent button, expand first task, verify nested. (6) Outdent test: click nested task's Outdent, verify returns to top-level. (7) Capture screenshot, report console errors."
      - working: false
        agent: "testing"
        comment: "❌ CRITICAL BUG FOUND (Oct 16, 2026 - Review Request): WBS List structure controls (Move Up/Down, Indent/Outdent) are NOT working correctly due to VISUAL ORDER vs LOGICAL ORDER MISMATCH. Test credentials: admin@test.com/admin123. Frontend URL: https://ddplanner-fixes.preview.emergentagent.com. Viewport: 1920x1080. Test project: Website Redesign (30 WBS tasks). ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED: The List view renders tasks using topoSortedTasks (topological sort by dependencies and start dates), but Move Up/Down operations use getSiblings() which sorts by the 'order' field. These two sorting methods produce DIFFERENT orders, causing the wrong tasks to be swapped. DETAILED ANALYSIS: (1) VISUAL ORDER (topoSortedTasks): Task 1 (ID: 6ab26109f81b3e3252a2600b) is followed by Task 3 (ID: 6ab26109f81b3e3252a2600f) in the UI. (2) LOGICAL ORDER (order field sort): Task 1 (ID: 6ab26109f81b3e3252a2600b) is followed by Task 6 (ID: 6ab26109f81b3e3252a26015) based on order field. (3) NETWORK ACTIVITY: When Move Down is clicked on Task 1, the API correctly swaps Task 1 with Task 6 (based on order field sort), NOT Task 3 (visual next sibling). Network log shows: PUT /api/wbs/tasks/6ab26109f81b3e3252a2600b (Task 1) and PUT /api/wbs/tasks/6ab26109f81b3e3252a26015 (Task 6) both returned 200. GET /api/projects/{project_id}/wbs refetch also returned 200. (4) UI DOES NOT UPDATE: After the swap, the UI still shows Task 1 followed by Task 3 because the visual order (topoSortedTasks) is unchanged. The order field swap doesn't affect the topological sort order. TEST RESULTS: ❌ Move Down FAILED: Clicked Move Down on Task 1, but visual order did NOT change. Task 1 and Task 3 remained in same positions. Expected: Task 3 to move above Task 1. Got: No visual change. ❌ Move Up: Since order didn't change, this test passed trivially (order was already the same). ❌ Indent FAILED: Clicked Indent on Task 3, but it was NOT nested under Task 1. All tasks still show 0px padding (all top-level). Expected: Task 3 to appear indented under Task 1 after expanding. Got: Task 3 remained at top-level with 0px padding. ✅ Outdent: Since Task 3 was never nested, it remained at top-level (trivial pass). CONSOLE ERRORS: ✅ No console errors detected. CODE ANALYSIS: (A) List View Rendering (WBSView.js line 1034): Uses topoSortedTasks.filter(t => !t.parent_id) to get root tasks. topoSortedTasks is computed via Kahn's algorithm with start_date tiebreaker (lines 365-440). (B) Move Up/Down Logic (WBSView.js lines 667-725): getSiblings() filters by parent_id and sorts by (a.order || 0) - (b.order || 0). handleMoveDown swaps order field values between siblings[index] and siblings[index+1]. (C) THE MISMATCH: Visual order is determined by topological sort (dependencies + dates), but Move operations work on order field sort. These are DIFFERENT orderings! IMPACT: Users see tasks in one order (topological), but Move Up/Down operations swap tasks in a different order (order field), making the controls appear broken. The UI doesn't update because the topological order is unchanged by order field swaps. FIX REQUIRED: The Move Up/Down operations should work on the VISUAL order (topoSortedTasks), not the order field sort. Options: (1) Change getSiblings() to return siblings in topoSorted order, OR (2) Change List view to render tasks sorted by order field instead of topoSortedTasks, OR (3) Update order field values to match topoSorted positions after each refetch. Screenshots: wbs_after_move_down.png, wbs_network_test.png. Test files: Playwright scripts in browser automation tool. RECOMMENDATION: Main agent should fix the visual order vs logical order mismatch by ensuring Move Up/Down operations work on the same order that users see in the List view."
